title: The semi-representable object of maps from a finite simplicial set
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $K$ a simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object], and $S$ a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with $S_n$ finite and nonempty for all $n\geq0$ and with finitely many nondegenerate simplices. For an object $W$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, an *$S$-family in $K$ over $W$* is a family of morphisms $f_s:W\to K_n$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, one for each $n\geq0$ and $s\in S_n$, with $K(\varphi)\circ f_s=f_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for every $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ and $s\in S_n$ (equivalently, a morphism of simplicial objects $W\times S\to K$, where $(W\times S)_n=\coprod_{s\in S_n}W$); composing with a morphism $W'\to W$ gives an $S$-family over $W'$. The object $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ is an object of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ with an $S$-family $(u_s)$ over it which is universal: for every $W$, $g\mapsto(u_s\circ g)_s$ is a bijection from morphisms $W\to\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ to $S$-families over $W$. It exists by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-exists] and is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the universal families. In particular, for an object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$ the $T$-points of $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ are the $S$-families over $\{T\}$: compatible families of $T$-points of the $K_n$, one for each simplex of $S$. For a simplicial subset $A\subseteq S$ satisfying the same hypotheses, restriction $(f_s)_{s\in S}\mapsto(f_s)_{s\in A}$ sends $S$-families to $A$-families compatibly with composition; the *restriction morphism* $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ is the unique morphism $\rho$ with $u^A_s\circ\rho=u^S_s$ for all $s\in A$.
